items.title: Portfolio Mapping
items.body: Classify and map large patent portfolios across technologies, applications, products and competitors. Understand how a technology is evolving and where your organisation stands within it. Map competitors, technical approaches, patent activity, and emerging areas to see where the market is concentrating investment and where gaps remain. Use that intelligence to validate R&D direction, anticipate competitive moves, and identify the technologies and opportunities worth pursuing.

items.title: Landscape Monitoring
items.body: Track a technology area continuously and be alerted the moment it shifts. Understand which competitors have entered, which applications have just published, and which technical approaches are accelerating — without rebuilding the analysis by hand each quarter. Set watches on specific technologies, companies or problem areas, and receive alerts as new filings publish, new entrants appear, or activity moves in an unexpected direction. Use that running view to catch competitive moves while there is still time to respond, and keep strategy current between formal reviews.

items.title: Technology Scouting
items.body: Describe a technical problem and search globally for the technologies, methods and materials that could solve it. Understand which approaches are already proven, which are still emerging, and who holds the capability behind each one. Scan patents, publications, startups, universities and established players, including industries that have solved the same underlying constraint for entirely different reasons. Use the resulting shortlist to source solutions externally, choose partners, and import proven approaches into a domain where they are still novel.

items.title: Concept Generation
items.body: Start from a technical problem and generate candidate solutions tested against both the published record and your own internal knowledge bases. Understand which approaches are genuinely new, which your teams have already tried, and why the ones that failed didn’t work. Use the surviving shortlist to develop a few concepts that stand up to the evidence, rather than repeating an experiment a colleague ran three years ago.

items.title: Reformulation
items.body: Take a product that already works and adapt it to a constraint it was never designed for, whether a restricted ingredient, a new market’s regulations, a supply shortage or a lower price point. Understand which substitutions are viable, how each is likely to affect performance, and which have already been tried across your own formulation history and the published literature. Use that to reach a small set of candidate reformulations worth taking to the bench, with the trade-offs understood before the first batch is produced.

items.title: Experiment Design
items.body: Bring together results held across ELNs, instrument outputs and historical project reports, and turn them into a single comparable picture of what your teams have already tested. Understand which parameters drive performance, where the data is thin, and which conditions remain untested. Use that to plan the experiments that resolve the most uncertainty per run, and to feed each result back so the next round is more precisely targeted than the last.

items.title: Knowledge Capture
items.body: Turn your organisation’s technical knowledge, standards, and ways of working into a shared intelligence layer. Ground every workflow in your internal context: from engineering documents and prior work to preferred methods, terminology, and quality expectations. As teams use Ankar, that knowledge compounds, making outputs more relevant, consistent, and specific to how your organisation innovates.

items.title: Patent Drafting
items.body: Every patent application begins with the same challenge: understanding what is truly inventive. Patent practitioners must sift through disclosures, technical documents, and inventor discussions to identify the core innovation. Ankar helps practitioners distill complex technical disclosures into defensible claim strategies, enabling faster drafting of stronger patent applications.

items.title: Prosecution
items.body: Aggregate prosecution history, prior art references, and examiner positions to identify the strongest path forward and respond with confidence. Map rejections onto specific claims to expose weaknesses in examiner reasoning, assess how similar rejections have been raised and overcome before, and uncover the arguments and amendments most likely to move prosecution forward. Turn this into a ready-to-file response, targeted at specific rejections and grounded in legal precedent.

items.title: Invalidity
items.body: Build stronger opposition strategies by bringing the patent, prosecution history, prior art, and existing arguments into a single analysis. Identify the most promising grounds for challenge, test claims against the strongest evidence, and develop structured arguments supported by precise citations. Move faster from initial assessment to a defensible opposition strategy.

items.title: Portfolio Pruning
items.body: Focus investment on the patents that matter most. Understand which assets protect current products, map to competitor activity, or remain strategically relevant, and identify patents that no longer justify their renewal cost. Bring evidence into portfolio decisions so teams can reduce unnecessary spend while preserving the assets that create real competitive advantage.
